payload.explanation: Monitor mon_e22a273ccf05 (effort_event, finger_joint, le 10, from u_brown raw_spec.limits.max_clamp_effort) fired during grasp_skill(object_id=u_brown, expected_width_m=0.02) within step pick_u_brown, triggering at 29.76 vs threshold 10. get_evidence over the grasp window (joint_states/finger_joint) shows effort was near-zero (~-0.03) through the finger closing sweep from -0.56 to ~0.58 rad, then jumped sharply at 0.5825 rad (5.13), 0.5875 rad (12.37), 0.5974 rad (29.76, the fire), continuing to climb to a peak of 76.67 at position 0.6309 before settling to a sustained plateau around 66.5. This is the signature of the gripper finger contacting the part and continuing to close/squeeze past first contact rather than stopping at a controlled grip force: a sharp effort spike concurrent with position still advancing, then a high sustained plateau nearly 7x the object's tolerated max_clamp_effort (10, per u_brown's raw_spec.limits.max_clamp_effort). I judge this a real overclamp on u_brown, not sensor noise or a mis-arming, because the threshold is read directly from u_brown's own contract and the plateau is sustained rather than a single transient tick.

Same mechanism as before: the gripper is sustaining a clamp force far above u_brown's tolerated max_clamp_effort of 10. I am not re-arming this absolute-threshold monitor again for this grasp, since the violation is already established and continuing to re-record identical readings adds no new information; it remains an open, uncorrected invariant breach through this hold.

Same mechanism as before -- not a new event, but the invariant was still being violated while this step was open, so it is recorded here too per-step. The violation ends with release_skill(u_brown) during this same step (phase 'released' at wall 1792110425036622000), after which the clamp effort ceases to apply to u_brown.

Same standing overclamp first established under pick_u_brown (peak 76.67 at grasp) continuing through the carry/approach: the gripper did not reduce clamp force after the initial over-squeeze. Recorded here because the invariant was open and violated while this step was in progress; it is the same physical mechanism as the pick_u_brown finding, not a new one.

payload.explanation: This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering all 12 steps of the expected process (all of which arrived under their mapped step_ids; no unplanned steps occurred). I measured each part's final pose against its own placement frame via query_snapshot after run_ended (status "completed"): u_brown 0.00216 m from u_brown_placement (tol 0.01), u_orange 0.00204 m from u_orange_placement (tol 0.02), line_green 0.00661 m from line_green_placement (tol 0.015), inverted_u_yellow 0.00149 m from inverted_u_yellow_placement (tol 0.012) -- all within tolerance. base1 and all five other-assembly bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) were checked against their run-start reference positions and found displaced by at most 0.0003 m, well under the 0.02 m disturbance tolerance, confirmed stationary across the entire run via continuously-armed stationarity monitors that never fired. Each part's own effects clauses (lift height, TCP tracking, grasp-effort plateau confirming contact, grasp-width error) passed at its milestone step, and in-hand-slippage relative_frame monitors never fired for any of the four parts, so no part slipped in the gripper. Each grasp closed on the correct named object per the grasp_skill events.\n\nDuring u_brown's handling (pick_u_brown, place_approach_u_brown, place_u_brown) the finger_joint clamp-effort invariant was violated repeatedly: effort spiked to 76.67 at the moment of grasp closure and plateaued around 48-66, nearly 5-7x u_brown's tolerated max_clamp_effort of 10 (from u_brown's own raw_spec.limits.max_clamp_effort). get_evidence over the grasp window showed the effort jump coincided with the gripper continuing to close past first contact rather than stopping at a controlled force, consistent with an over-squeeze on a comparatively low-tolerance part (u_brown's limit of 10 is far below u_orange's 200, line_green's 170, and inverted_u_yellow's 250, so the same closing behavior that was safe on the other three parts exceeded u_brown's specific bound). This was recorded as three non_conformant findings (one per step it was open in) via record_verdict. The violation resolved itself when release_skill(u_brown) fired at the end of place_u_brown -- after release the clamp effort no longer applies to u_brown, and u_brown's final seated pose is within tolerance and was never displaced afterward (confirmed unchanged across all three subsequent part placements). No standing violation remains at run end: the overclamp was a transient, now-corrected departure, not an uncorrected one, so this is a RECOVERY rather than a non_conformant end-state. All four parts reached their required end states within tolerance and no violation stands, so the run verdict is conformant.
